title: The rank and layer distributions in random recursive trees
summary: The distribution of node depths in a network is crucial for analyzing network structure. Two measures, rank and layer, quantify how deep inside a network a node is. The rank is the node's distance to the closest leaf, a node of degree 1. The layer is the number of times all leaves must be stripped off for the node to become a leaf. We derive exact recursive expressions for the rank and layer distributions in random recursive trees.
